Commentary.Commentary: That is it from this game! The Windies just showed why they are the World Champions in this format with an impressive performance. However, cricket is the real winner in the end. The sport though continues as England will face Pakistan in the second Test on the 1st of June. Not to forget they are 1-0 down in the series. So that promises to be another exciting clash. We would love your company. Do join us for that. Till then, take care and goodbye.
Evin Lewis has been named the Man of the Match for his blazing 58 which laid the foundation for the Windies to post a big first innings total.

So a convincing win for the Windies. It was all set up by their batsmen in the first half and their bowlers too did a very good job. Chasing 200, the World XI's innings never took off. They lost four wickets in the Powerplay with Badree and Russell taking two each. Thisara Perera was the lone fighter as he notched up a half ton but that was never going to be enough. Kesrick Williams was impressive at the death as he finished with a three-fer.

OUT! In the air... and that is another exceptional catch! Nurse is the man this time. Fuller ball on off, McClenaghan swings but only manages to hit it high up in the air. There were quite a few fielders converging towards the ball but Nurse who runs in from sweeper cover, calls for it and takes it diving forward. They go upstairs to check for the no ball but the bowler has not overstepped. Smiles in the Windies camp as THEY HAVE WON BY 72 RUNS!
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman. The batsmen have run through for a single.

A huge appeal but not given! McClenaghan goes for a reverse sweep but misses to get hit on the pads. The bowler appeals but the umpire shakes his head. Pitching outside leg. The umpire has not signaled it as a leg bye so there might be an inside edge.
A yorker on middle, Sandeep jams it out to long on for a run.
SIX! He has picked the bones out of that one. Goes down on one knee and nails the slog sweep. It sails over the mid-wicket fence. End of a big over. 76 needed from 24.
FOUR BYES! Turn again! A similar delivery to the last one. This time it turns even more. The keeper fails to collect as Mitchell misses his shot and the ball rolls into the third man fence.
Turn! This is floated up on off, Mitchell swings, he is beaten by the turn.
A yorker on off, Sandeep swings but it goes off the bottom edge towards short third man for a run.
Fires it outside off, Lamichhane tries to cut but misses.

A full toss on the pads, Mitchell tries to flick but gets an inside edge onto his pads. The ball rolls towards the leg side. They first think of a single but then hesitate but eventually go for it and complete it. The umpire signals it as a leg bye, so there was no inside edge there.
Slower delivery to end the over from Williams. The batsman looks to play it fine, gets an under edge and gets a single.
Full and slow and Mitchell manages to punch it down the wicket. They take two off the second last delivery of the over.
The batsman has driven it through mid-on from the inside half of his bat. One run added to the total.
Sandeep Lamichhane walks out to the middle. This will be the last wicket as Mills will not be coming out to bat due to the injury he suffered while fielding.

OUT! This looked plumb and the umpire agrees with the bowler. A little cameo from Rashid Khan ends. He was looking to tickle the fuller delivery fine by moving right across his stumps but doesn't get any bat on it. The ball crashes into his pads, in front of his stumps and it's bye bye to the Afghan magician.

SIX! He isn't going to get bogged down with dismissals at the other end. Goes deep in his crease, gets a shortish delivery and swings his bat hard, gets a top edge and the ball flies over square leg boundary. Half a dozen added to the total.
Wide! Rashid leaves the wide delivery and the umpire signals wide.
Mitchell McClenaghan walks out to the middle.

OUT! WHAT A CATCH! These skyscrapers are never easy but Williams has managed to hold onto it. And with that, the last ray of WXI's hope is also walking back. Perera has played a good innings but couldn't get his team to the end. Coming to the delivery, he bowls it slow, on a goodish length and the batsman wanted to hit it out of the park but could only manage a top edge. The ball went high in the air, towards the vacant mid on region and Williams sprints back to take a stunner. Windies are going through the WXI batsmen without breaking any sweat. ICC World XI have lost their seventh wicket.
Kesrick Williams in back into the attack.
Fuller one into the pads but Rashid doesn't get bat on it.
The batsman has driven it straight down the ground.
Almost got yorked with the slower delivery. Manages to get an inside edge and the ball goes down the fine leg. One run added to the total.
The batsman rocks onto the backfoot and punches the ball to cover.
Short and outside off and the batsman goes over covers. Lewis sticks his boot in time and saves a couple for his team.

One run. A half tracker from Nurse to start with. Rashid gets a good connection as he lofts it towards the wid-wicket boundary. The fielder runs in from the boundary to go for the catch, reaches it in time but couldn't hold onto it. The ball hits him in his leg and stays inside the rope. A lucky break for the leggie!
Ashley Nurse is into the attack.
Fuller on off, Khan hits it down to long off for a run.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.
Squeezes this towards point. The fielder has a needless shy at the non-striker's end and misses. The batsmen run an overthrow.
Fuller on off, Perera eases it down to long off for a run.
Rashid Khan strides out to the middle.

OUT! Afridi holes out! Paul bowls a low full toss on the pads. Such deliveries are never easy to put away. Afridi tries to clear the mid-wicket fence but does not get the desired distance. It goes straight into the hands of the fielder, Ashley Nurse, who takes it easily. An uncharacteristic innings by Shahid comes to an end. He gets a standing ovation as he walks back as this could PROBABLY be the last time he walks off in an international game.
A yorker to begin with. Perera tries to jam it out but it goes off the inner half towards mid-wicket for a run.
Keemo Paul is back on.
Full and outside off and Afridi does well to reach the ball but gets an under edge on it.
It's been driven superbly through the covers. They pick up a single.
FOUR! Goes short and surprises Perera. He goes for the pull and the top edge flies over the fine leg fielder for a boundary.
FOUR! Fifty for Perera! He is keeping his team in the contest. Slower delivery, outside off and he does to get past the running cover fielder.
Full and on the pads and Perera flicks it to mid-wicket as they take two.
Loft it over mid off but doesn't get the connection. One run added to the total.
Andre Russell back into the attack.

On a goodish length, into his pads and Afridi gets his bat down in time. It hits the inside edge of the bat and deflects onto his pads. The ball rolls towards the third man fielder and they take a quick single amidst some confusion.
Wide! Similar delivery and similar result.
Wide! Goes too wide and umpire stretches his arms to signal wide.
Yorker from the bowler and Afridi misses it as he is looking to cut the ball.
On a shortish length on the stumps and the batsman does well to punch the ball to mid on for a single.

SIX! WOW! Cleanly hits this one! Williams goes full and into the arch of Perera who lofts it over long off for another maximum. Back-to-back sixes for the left hander. He needs to stay in the middle for the sake of WXI.
SIX! Too short and too much width for Perera. He isn't going to miss out on his favourite scoring shot. Picks the shot ball early and puts it way back in to the crowd at mid-wicket.
Wide outside off from the bowler and Afridi does well to dab the ball to the point region. One run added to the total.
Kesrick Williams is back on.
Full and outside off, Perera squeezes it out to the fielder at covers.
SIX! They need a lot more! Another short ball on middle, Perera this time gets hold of it as he pulls it over square leg for half a dozen.
Swing and a miss! Good length outside off, Perera throws the kitchen sink at it but misses.
Down the leg side and the umpire signals it a wide.
Goes fuller on middle, Afridi works it through mid-wicket for a run.
Shortish on the body of the batsman. He goes for a pull but gets an inside edge down to fine leg for a run.
Length ball on middle, Perera pulls it to mid-wicket.
Driven through mid on by the batsman. They pick up a single.
Edged but a run! Full outside off, Shahid swings but gets an outside edge down to third man for a run.
Eased down to long on for a run.
A yorker outside off, Parera swings but misses.
On the off stump, Afridi tries to work it on the off side but gets it off the inner half towards mid-wicket for a run.

FOUR! Could have easily been a wicket had the fielder been at the ropes. Afridi walks across the stumps and flicks it towards fine leg. The fielder there is standing well inside the ropes. The ball goes over his head and into the fence.
On the pads, Afirdi tucks it around the corner for a run.
Good length on off, blocked.
Shahid Afridi comes out to bat and he has not come alone here. He comes out with a runner.

OUT! Just as a partnership started to build, the Windies have broken through. Half the side back in hut for the World XI! Brathwaite strikes in his first over! He goes wide of the crease and angles it onto the off pole. It jags back in after pitching. Malik plays down the wrong line and gets hit on the pads. The players appeal and the umpire raises his finger. 155 more needed.
Malik makes room and Brathwaite follows him. He works it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Good length on middle, Perera swings but gets an inside edge down to third man for a run.
Starts off with a length ball outside off, Malik guides it down to third man and gets to the other end.
Carlos Brathwaite is into the attack.

FOUR! He is looking to play it over the mid-wicket region and this time he gets the delivery he wanted. A short ball, into his body and the batsman pulls it hard to end the over with another boundary.

FOUR! Low, dipping full toss, outside off and Perera does well to get his bat on the ball. The ball skids through the turf and the fielder at wide mid off couldn't get to it. A welcome boundary for the Sri Lankan!
Goes for the biggie but doesn't get the connection. The ball rolls to the mid-wicket fielder.
Presents the full face of the bat and defends it to the off side and starts running. Perera had to scamper for the single. In the end, no harm done.
Goes short and into the batsman. The batsman pulls but mistimes it to mid-wicket. It was in the air but away from the reach of the fielder.
Full on middle and Malik strokes it to the mid-wicket region for a single.
Keemo Paul is into the attack.
Slower ball, coming into the batsman and Perera does well to check his drive as he nearly chipped it to the mid-wicket fielder.
The batsman rocks onto the backfoot and punches the ball.

OOH! Almost, almost hits the stumps. Bowls it on a short of good length, angling into the left hander. Perera goes to his leg side to play it through covers but misses the ball but the ball goes past the off stump, a touch too close for the batsman.
FOUR! Perera's cricket is sorted out. He doesn't move too much in his crease and picks the shortish delivery over the point fielder for another boundary.
Played to the point region by the batsman. They pick up a single.

FOUR! WOW! Class from Malik! This was bowled on a short of a length, angling in to the right hander and Malik gets on his toes and punches it off the back foot to the cover boundary. Beautiful timing from the Pakistan international.
Wide! Another repeat of the previous delivery.
Wide! Kesrick Williams into the attack and bowls it down the leg.
Floated on leg stump and Malik tickles it for a single.
Comes down the track to smother the spin. Gets his bat and pad closer to dab the ball to cover.
Leg bye! On his pads and the batsman gets hit on his pad. Another run added to the total.
Touch closer to the bat of the left-hander who misses the ball once again.
Faster one from the leggie, outside off and Perera misses the cut.
Flighted outside off and Malik dabs it to the mid on region for a single.
FOUR! Through the on side this time. Russell bangs it in short, Perera rocks back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
FOUR! Off the mark in style! Short ball and outside off, Perera says thank you so much as he cuts it over point and the ball races away.

OUT! They are falling like a pack of cards here. Billings is the latest to take the long walk back. The short ball does the trick. Russell bends his back on this one and bangs it short on middle. Billings tries to pull but is done in by the bounce. He gets a top edge towards Brathwaite at mid on who accepts an easy catch. Thisara Perera is the next man in.
Back of a length on off, Billings defends it onto the ground.
Fuller on off, it is driven to covers.
Shoaib Malik walks out to the middle.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! Karthik bags a duck and the task now for World XI chasing this total down has been dented further. A short ball by Badree. Karthik goes for the pull but gets a top edge which lobs onto the off side. Lewis at point takes his second catch. End of a double-wicket maiden for Badree.
Another attempt to sweep but once again the ball hits Karthik on the pads. He has not got going here.
On the pads again, Karthik goes down on one knee and tries to sweep but misses to get hit on the pads.
Fires it on the pads, Karthik tries to work it on the leg side but misses. The players appeal but the umpire is not interested.
Flatter on off, it is pushed to the man at point.
Dinesh Karthik is the next man in.

OUT! Badree gets his man this time! Once again just like the one in Badree's last over, this was plumb and this time the umpire raises his finger. This was quicker and on the shorter side. Ronchi rocks back and goes for the pull. He misses and the ball hits him on the pads. The players appeal and the umpire raises his finger. Badree is pumped up and World XI are in big trouble here.
FOUR! Easy picking for the Local Lad. He gets a full toss on his pads and flicks it to the mid-wicket boundary to open his account.
Shortish delivery from the bowler and Billing does well to defend it off the back foot.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

OUT! Excellent take by Lewis! Russell gets his first but a lot of credit has to be given to Lewis here. Tamim makes room and gets a full ball on middle. He drives it square on the off side and he seems to have timed it well. It goes towards point where Lewis times his jump to perfection, stretches his hands up and takes it. Tamim walks back in disbelief and an early wicket for Windies, just the start they would have hoped for with the ball.
Punches it off the back foot but no power in the shot. The ball goes straight back to the bowler.
Drives but doesn't get the connection.
Russell starts with a wide. Goes too wide of the off stump.
Andre Russell will bowl from the other end.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Shuffles across his stumps to force the shot, gets an inside edge on to his pads.
Plants his foot down the pitch and drives it to cover but finds the fielder. Tamim will be disappointed there, it was a half-volley. He should have put that away.

Floated on the middle, Ronchi tries to go across the line and misses the delivery as it hits his pad. The Windies team appeals in unison but the umpire is not interested. The replays shows the ball would have crashed into the leg stump but luckily for Ronchi no reviews available in this game. They take a single in all that chaos.
Similar delivery from Badree. The batsman flicks it to the mid-wicket region and takes a single.
Starts with a shortish delivery on the pads. Tamim flicks it off his pads.

We are back for the chase! A huge task is what awaits the World XI side as their two batters, Tamim Iqbal and Luke Ronchi make their way out to the middle. We have to spin to start with by Windies, Samuel Badree has the new ball in hand. Here we go...
